evidence.text: The article reports the earliest known 文 forms in Late Shang oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions, describing standing human-shaped graphs similar to 大, with chest marks that vary or are absent. It traces the marks through reduction to dots or short strokes and eventual disappearance in later forms. It reports early use in personal and place names, especially as an honorific modifier in Shang royal names, followed by Western Zhou royal posthumous names and ancestor honorifics. These are the article’s summaries; its inscriptional examples were not independently checked against primary editions here.
evidence.title: 甲骨和金文的「文」字真的和「文身」有關嗎？

evidence.text: The article reviews tattoo and other chest-mark interpretations, as well as Liu Yuan’s proposal that 文 could correspond to 大 and mean ‘great’ in some Shang uses. Its author favors the ‘great’ analysis but acknowledges that it does not explain the chest mark. The article therefore documents a live disagreement; it does not establish that the graph originally meant ‘tattoo’ or ‘great’. Its proposed semantic developments to writing, literature, and culture are not independently dated by the evidence inspected.
evidence.title: 甲骨和金文的「文」字真的和「文身」有關嗎？

evidence.text: The 文 evolution page indexes oracle-bone, bronze-inscription, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen forms. The page establishes the script categories indexed, but does not itself establish what the early chest marks depict or mean.
evidence.title: 漢字「文」：字形演變

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi text and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: Xu Shen’s entry explains 文 as 「錯畫也。象交文。凡文之屬皆从文。」 Duan Yucai’s commentary interprets the account in terms of intersecting patterns. This is an early Han interpretation of the seal form, not direct evidence of the Shang graph’s referent.
evidence.kind: historical lexicographic text with later commentary
evidence.title: 說文解字「文」

Its file history identifies the source as a Ritsumeikan University Shirakawa gallery SVG. The page states the representation is public domain and links the original SVG. It is a modern vector image, not an ancient artifact photograph.

gaps: The precise earliest inscriptional instance and its date were not independently checked against primary editions or artifact facsimiles. The CASE article reports Late Shang attestations and examples; the Academia Sinica index identifies script categories but does not settle interpretation.

The chest marks’ referent and the earliest sense remain disputed. Tattooing, other marking interpretations, and the 文/大 ‘great’ analysis are competing accounts; none is established here as the certain origin.

The dossier’s gloss sequence from marking or ‘great’ to pattern, writing, literature, and culture is not supported by dated semantic links in the sources inspected. Do not infer chronology from the modern gloss list.
The proposed claim that 文 is the graphic original of 紋 and the proposed derivation from 煤 were not independently substantiated.
The supplied local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows were not needed for a sound-component analysis because no sound component is proposed. They do not establish graphic origin or semantic chronology.
The Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang character query returned HTTP 401 in the supplied packet; no Xiaoxuetang image or rights notice was used.

The supplied oracle, bronze, and seal image candidates returned HTTP 404 and were excluded. One alternate Commons oracle-script vector was verified and selected. No primary inscription photograph was selected; the chosen image is a modern vector depiction.
No small local extract is recommended: permission and editorial value for a repeated source corpus were not both established.

items.period: Shang oracle-script style; exact inscriptional date not specified for this redraw
items.caption: Modern vector depiction of 文 in oracle-script style. Early forms are reported as human-shaped, with chest marks that vary or may be absent; their referent remains disputed.
items.alt: Modern vector drawing of an oracle-script form of 文.
items.selection_reason: Provides a usable, rights-verified alternate after the supplied oracle redraw candidate failed acquisition. It illustrates the broad script category discussed in the research, without presenting the drawing as an artifact photograph or resolving the graph’s debated interpretation.
items.rights: Public domain statement on the exact Commons file page; the page says the creator released rights generated by making the SVG.

limitations.text: This is a modern vector depiction, not a photograph or facsimile of a particular excavated inscription. Its page cites reference databases and a Ritsumeikan Shirakawa gallery SVG as source; the specific glyph was not independently compared with a primary artifact image here.
The chest-mark referent and whether the graph’s early sense was ‘tattoo’, ‘great’, or another value remain unresolved in the inspected sources.
